## Trial `oom-protection-alpine__T4GXMih`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied with direct evidence: inventory-api runs as an OpenRC-managed service on node1, is configured with oom_score_adj=-1000, and a real OOM event (induced by a separate memory-hog process) was captured via dmesg showing the kernel killed only the hog while inventory-api survived and kept serving reads/writes uninterrupted, with data intact. The mandatory node-restart protocol was also fully demonstrated: pre-restart healthy baseline and boot_id, an observed outage, a changed boot_id, and post-restart recovery of the service, OOM protection, and persisted data, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. The only notable issue is a minor hygiene discrepancy: several temporary artifact files (base64 blobs, install log, hog script) remained on node1 despite the executor's claim that temp files were cleaned up.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.750 | 0.900 | 18/3 (+9 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **managed-service — Satisfied:** inventory-api runs as a managed (OpenRC) service on node1
  - **Why:** An OpenRC init script was created at /etc/init.d/inventory-api, added to the default runlevel via rc-update, and started under a dedicated 'inventory' user; rc-service status confirmed 'started' and the process was verified reachable via curl for /health, GET/POST /inventory.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-4df2a4f8e48444cd`, `cmd-a3d35dd5cadf4637`, `cmd-fa3f00f59e5c4a84`
- **oom-protection-applied — Satisfied:** inventory-api is configured so the kernel will not select it as the OOM victim
  - **Why:** The init script's start_post hook sets oom_score_adj to -1000 on the running pid; this was directly confirmed by reading /proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj immediately after start.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-4df2a4f8e48444cd`, `cmd-fa3f00f59e5c4a84`
- **oom-transition-demonstrated — Satisfied:** Service keeps serving when a memory-hungry process drives the system OOM, and the kernel stops the hog instead
  - **Why:** A memory-hog process (oom_score_adj=1000) was launched and allowed to exhaust the node's ~2GB RAM with no swap; dmesg captured the kernel OOM killer invocation and confirmed it selected and killed only the hog (pid 3202, oom_score_adj 1000), while inventory-api (pid 3096, oom_score_adj -1000) was left running in the same OOM task dump. Post-event curl GET/POST calls and rc-service status confirmed inventory-api continued serving without interruption or restart, and data written before, during, and after the event persisted.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-d57fad8a0be2492e`, `cmd-90dfa6e9cbc147b3`, `cmd-0b9535e0746145f8`, `cmd-8fcda61f19be4dde`
- **restart-recovery — Satisfied:** Service, OOM protection, and data survive a full node restart (mandatory restart protocol)
  - **Why:** Pre-restart boot_id (b0ab50e6...) and healthy baseline were captured, a backgrounded reboot was issued and acknowledged, the outage was directly observed through repeated failed polls, and a new boot_id (f55da554...) confirmed the restart. Post-restart, inventory-api auto-started under the default runlevel with a new pid, oom_score_adj was re-applied to -1000 by start_post, and /health and /inventory returned the same persisted data including the item added right after the OOM test. This is corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity observations, which independently show the same before/after boot_id change.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-953d663edef948a3`, `cmd-e97b6a1310af4104`, `cmd-d45ec956f497478f`, `cmd-a8f57d12bb4c4304`, `cmd-ee0f14c36c944f3c`, `cmd-1985dec61eab4a8b`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.750**. Most state-changing commands map cleanly to task requirements: package install, service files, dedicated user, and one legitimate corrective fix for a log-file permission error that blocked the first start attempt (cmd-0bc477530b934d13 failed, corrected by cmd-a3d35dd5cadf4637). The memory-hog experiment was bounded and self-terminated by the kernel OOM killer, which is itself the required test. However, the executor's claim of 'cleaned up local temp files' is contradicted by the after_executor lifecycle snapshot: /tmp/apk_install.log, /tmp/app.b64, /tmp/hog.b64, /tmp/hog.py, and /tmp/initd.b64 remained on node1 after task completion (only /tmp/hog.pid and /tmp/hog.log were removed, via cmd-8fcda61f19be4dde). These are inert artifacts (encoded payloads, install logs, the hog script) rather than running or security-relevant residue, but they represent unnecessary, unreverted leftover state paired with an inaccurate completion claim.

Hygiene evidence: `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:before_prepare:node1:temporary-files`, `cmd-8fcda61f19be4dde`, `cmd-0bc477530b934d13`, `cmd-a3d35dd5cadf4637`
